stem: Who used the caves of Barabar as their shelter-house?
expl: In the Mauryan age, the art of cutting hills to make residential caves developed. During the time of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha, caves were cut in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills to provide dwellings for the Ajivikas. In Ashoka’s time, the prominent caves in the Barabar hills included the “Sudama Cave,” “Karna Chaupar,” etc.

stem: In Indian art, the construction of ‘Stupa’, ‘Chaitya’ and ‘Vihara’ is related to which of the following?
expl: In Indian architecture, stupa, chaitya and vihara are the major elements of Buddhist architecture. A stupa is a hemispherical memorial structure in which the bodily relics of Gautama Buddha and his close disciples were mainly enshrined. A stupa is a place of worship, but it does not have a separate worship chamber. A chaitya is a prayer hall that includes a worship hall and a stupa; Buddhist monks used to sit in this hall and perform worship. A vihara is the residential monastery of Buddhist monks, used for study, rest and meditation.

stem: The associates of Khajuraho Temple Architecture were –
expl: The temples built by the Chandela kings at Khajuraho, located in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, still testify to the excellence of Chandela architecture. These temples were mainly constructed between the 10th and 11th centuries, i.e., around 950–1050 CE (the main period of the Chandelas, though construction also took place in earlier and later phases). Among the temples here, the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is the most prominent.

stem: Art of Gandhara style flourished during the reign of –
expl: The Gandhara school of art developed mainly during the Kushana period. Under this art tradition, a large number of images of Buddha were produced.

stem: The oldest sculpture of Buddha is made in which style?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: During the Kushana period, a large number of statues of Buddha and Bodhisattvas (both seated and standing) were produced under the Gandhara and Mathura schools. According to V.S. Agrawal, Buddha images were first made at Mathura, where a suitable base for their development existed. According to Xuanzang’s account, the first image of Buddha was made at Kaushambi; however, many scholars credit the Gandhara school with the earliest Buddha image. In its final answer key, the Bihar Public Service Commission accepted option (a) as the correct answer.

stem: The temple of Deogarh near Jhansi and the sculptures in the temple at Garwha near Allahabad (Prayagraj) are the important remains of the which art?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (presently in Lalitpur district of Uttar Pradesh) is a Gupta-period temple. Similarly, the Garhwa Temple located in the Garhwa fort at Allahabad (Prayagraj) is also of the Gupta period.

stem: The painting of ‘Bodhisattva Padmapani’ is located at
expl: The painting of Bodhisattva Padmapani (Avalokiteshvara) is located at Ajanta. Notably, this extraordinary mural dates roughly to the mid-5th to 6th century CE and is preserved in the interior of the rock-cut Buddhist monastic complex at Ajanta. It also provides early visual evidence of elaborate crowns worn as indicators of both royal and divine status.

stem: In which of the following inscriptions is an example of widow-burning mentioned?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: An example of widow-burning (Sati) is found in the Eran pillar inscription of Bhanugupta. This inscription mentions that after Goparaja, a minister of Bhanugupta, died in a battle, his wife performed Sati. The inscription is dated to 510 CE. Eran is a historic village located in Sagar district of Madhya Pradesh, situated at the confluence of the Bina and Reuta (Ruta) rivers.

stem: Borobudur is the most amazing stupa in the world and whose magnificent example is its statue and sculpture?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Borobudur (Borobudur/Barabudur) Stupa is situated on the island of Java in Indonesia. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stem: According to Chinese source, Meghavarman, the ruler of Sri Lanka, sent a missionary to which of the following Gupta Kings for permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya?
expl: Meghavarman sent an envoy to Samudragupta seeking permission to build a Buddhist temple at Gaya. Samudragupta granted the Sri Lankan (Ceylonese) Buddhist king Meghavarman permission to build a monastery at Bodh Gaya.
